item_name: ToMP (Mayer et al. CVPR 2022) - predicting target-model parameters with a Transformer instead of optimisation
bibliography: Christoph Mayer, Martin Danelljan, Goutam Bhat, Matthieu Paul, Danda Pani Paudel, Fisher Yu, Luc Van Gool. Transforming Model Prediction for Tracking. CVPR 2022, pp. 8731-8740 [uncertain page range]. arXiv:2203.11192 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11192). Code and models: PyTracking, https://github.com/visionml/pytracking - network ltr/models/tracking/tompnet.py, tracker parameters pytracking/parameter/tomp/tomp50.py (and tomp101.py). arXiv and CVPR versions are the same study. Directly related: SuperDiMP (PyTracking, baseline in Table 4), KeepTrack (Mayer et al. ICCV 2021, item N01), STARK (item N09).
full_text_checked: Full arXiv PDF text extracted and read: Sections 1-5 including Sections 3.1-3.5 (method, training, online tracking), 4.1 ablation with Tables 1-4, 4.2 comparisons Tables 5-8, 4.3 limitations. Supplementary Sec. A (architecture/training details, centerness study) not read. Code: tompnet.py existence and tomp50.py online parameters (search_area_scale 5, conf_ths 0.9, target_not_found_threshold 0.25, distractor_threshold 0.8, hard_negative_threshold 0.5, search_area_rescaling_at_occlusion True) read via raw GitHub; training not executed.
task_and_output: Generic single-object tracking from a first-frame box. Output per frame: target classification score map (18x18) from a predicted DCF filter applied to Transformer-enhanced test features; center = arg-max; a dense ltrb box map queried at the center gives the box. Online flags inherited from the DiMP tracker code (not_found / uncertain / hard_negative) via thresholds in tomp50.py.
data_and_independent_videos: Training: LaSOT, GOT10k, TrackingNet and MS-COCO training splits; 40k sub-sequences per epoch, 300 epochs; each sub-sequence = 2 training frames + 1 test frame sampled from a 200-frame window. Evaluation on separate test videos: LaSOT test (280), LaSOTExtSub (150 videos, 15 new classes, small fast objects with distractors), TrackingNet test (511, server), UAV123 (123), OTB-100 (100), NFS-30 (100), VOT2020 ST (60). Ablations (Tables 1-4) are run on LaSOT, NFS, OTB (and UAV, LaSOTExtSub in Table 4) test sets, i.e. on the reporting sets; no separate validation split reported.
target_size_and_input_resolution: Search area scale factor 5.0 relative to the target box; score map 18x18 (stride 16 implies roughly a 288x288 patch [uncertain]); same spatial resolution for training and test frames (unlike STARK/TransT small templates). Backbone ResNet-50 or ResNet-101 on RGB.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: Native benchmark frame rates (mostly 25-30 fps; NFS 30 fps version). Camera and background motion present in the benchmarks, not ablated. Training samples frames up to 200 frames apart.
detector_and_exemplar: No detector. Exemplar = annotated first frame (always kept) plus at most one previous frame whose classifier confidence exceeds a threshold (conf_ths 0.9 in tomp50.py), replaced by the most recent such frame. Two-stage inference: target classifier weights predicted from first frame + previous frame; box-regression weights predicted from the annotated first frame only (via key-padding mask).
trainable_nodes_and_loss: End-to-end trained: ResNet backbone, target-location encoding (learned foreground embedding e_fg multiplied by a Gaussian at the target center), target-extent encoding (MLP on dense ltrb distances), test-frame embedding e_test, Transformer encoder (joint self-attention over 2 training frames + test frame) and decoder (query = e_fg) that outputs the weights w; a linear layer splits w into classifier weights w_cls (1 x C, applied as a 1x1 DCF filter on encoder test features) and box weights w_bbreg (attention map conditioning a CNN box head). Loss: L = 100 * DiMP target classification loss (separate foreground/background treatment, hinge on background) + 1 * generalized IoU loss on ltrb boxes; no centerness loss. AdamW lr 1e-4, decay 0.2 at epochs 150 and 250, weight decay 1e-4, two Titan RTX GPUs. Parameter counts not reported in the main paper.
controls_seeds_splits: Table 1: target-state encoding variants (e_fg zero vs learned, learned background embedding e_bg, e_test, extent encoding phi on/off, decoder query shared with e_fg or separate), 7 rows. Table 2: one decoder query + linear layer vs two queries. Table 3: inference settings (only initial frame; previous frame + two-stage; previous frame without two-stage). Table 4: step-by-step transformation from SuperDiMP (DiMP optimiser predictor + probabilistic IoUNet) -> ToMP predictor for the classifier only -> ToMP for classifier and box. Matched baseline in Table 4 trained by the authors in the same framework. Seeds: single training run per variant; the paper states 5 runs are averaged only for trackers using the stochastic probabilistic IoUNet. No confidence intervals.
metrics_and_numbers: All success AUC %. Table 1 (LaSOT / NFS / OTB): row 1 e_fg = 0, extent only 66.0 / 64.8 / 68.2; row 2 67.1 / 66.6 / 70.0; row 3 67.1 / 66.3 / 69.4; row 4 final (e_fg + e_test + phi, shared query) 67.6 / 66.9 / 70.1; row 5 with learned background embedding 67.4 / 66.0 / 69.5; row 6 separate decoder query 66.0 / 66.2 / 69.9; row 7 without extent encoding phi 63.1 / 64.2 / 64.0. Table 2: one query + linear 67.6 / 66.9 / 70.1 vs two queries 63.7 / 62.8 / 67.9. Table 3: only initial frame 65.7 / 65.3 / 67.8; previous frame + two-stage 67.6 / 66.9 / 70.1; previous frame without two-stage 62.0 / 64.8 / 62.8 (-5.6 on LaSOT). Table 4 (LaSOT / NFS / UAV / LaSOTExtSub): DiMP optimiser + Prob. IoUNet (SuperDiMP) 63.1 / 64.8 / 67.7 / 43.7; ToMP predictor + Prob. IoUNet 64.7 / 65.2 / 65.0 / 45.2; ToMP + ToMP box 67.6 / 66.9 / 69.0 / 45.4. State of the art: LaSOT (Table 5) ToMP-101 68.5, ToMP-50 67.6, KeepTrack 67.1, STARK-ST101 67.1, SuperDiMP 63.1, PrDiMP 59.8; LaSOTExtSub (Fig. 5b) KeepTrack 48.2, ToMP-101 45.9, ToMP-50 45.4, SuperDiMP 43.7, LTMU 41.4; TrackingNet (Table 6) ToMP-101 81.5, ToMP-50 81.2, STARK-ST101 82.0; UAV123 (Table 7) ToMP-101 66.9, ToMP-50 69.0, KeepTrack 69.7; NFS ToMP-101 66.7, ToMP-50 66.9, KeepTrack 66.4; OTB ToMP 70.1; VOT2020 ST (Table 8) EAO ToMP-101 0.309, ToMP-50 0.297, STARK-ST101 0.308, SuperDiMP 0.305. Speed: 19.6 fps (ResNet-101), 24.8 fps (ResNet-50) on RTX 2080Ti.
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: yes (test splits; LaSOTExtSub with unseen classes). Target absence: not reported as a measured condition (out-of-view frames exist in LaSOT; per-attribute gains for Out-of-View and Full Occlusion shown in Fig. 4 only as AUC gains vs other trackers). Similar distractors: partially - LaSOTExtSub and UAV123 contain distractors; no dedicated distractor metric; authors state in Sec. 4.3 that distractors present while the target is occluded are a typical failure of ToMP because it lacks explicit distractor handling (KeepTrack beats it on LaSOTExtSub 48.2 vs 45.9). Occlusion: only via LaSOT attributes (Fig. 4), no separate evaluation. Night or low light: not reported (Illumination Variation attribute in Fig. 4 only). Sequential operation on own predictions: yes - the previous-frame memory uses the tracker's own predictions; Table 3 shows that feeding own predicted boxes to the box predictor degrades performance (-5.6 LaSOT), hence the two-stage scheme.
mechanism_summary: Published mechanism: replace DiMP's optimisation-based model predictor by a learned feed-forward predictor. Training-frame deep features are tagged with where the target is (Gaussian x learned foreground embedding) and how large it is (ltrb distance encoding); test-frame features are tagged with a test embedding; a Transformer encoder processes all frames jointly (so the test frame contributes transductively and features become target-aware), and the decoder, queried by the same foreground embedding, outputs the weights of a 1x1 DCF classifier and of a box-regression conditioning vector. Memory: the first annotated frame plus one most-recent high-confidence frame; the box predictor sees only the annotated frame to avoid self-reinforcing box errors. Proposed modification for us (not published): none recommended for implementation; the only transferable design lessons are (a) separate trusted vs pseudo-labelled exemplars per output (use own pseudo-labels for localisation only, not for extent/box), and (b) a learned predictor beats an optimiser only when trained on very large data.
transfer_limits: (1) Data and capacity: the Transformer predictor needs 300 epochs x 40k sub-sequences on four large datasets; we have ~130 train videos and 734 core parameters; a learned weight predictor would be a large external head trained on few episodes, i.e. our pre-trained exemplar matcher with absent class, which already failed to beat the readout. (2) Features: the predictor works on 1024/2048-channel RGB ResNet features with global self-attention over 18x18x3 tokens; FlyVis gives 34 motion/brightness channels on 721 hexals in a crop about 2x target - too few tokens and channels for attention-based discrimination to be expected. (3) Distractors: the paper itself names distractors during occlusion as a typical failure, which is exactly our Z13 case (find the previous target among similar neighbours after loss). (4) Time: memory of only first + one recent frame; our episodes have 4 exemplar observations and up to 30 lost frames at 30 Hz; transductive use of the current search frame is possible causally. (5) Environment: SOT box output, not association; our entry point is the center correction before ByteTrack/MASA matching. (6) Boundary: a Transformer weight predictor would be a new external module; it counts as FlyVis modernisation only if it replaces the readout node of the fly path and its gain is shown with FlyVis features vs input-eye features.
research_questions_addressed: 5.2 (target model and memory): direct evidence that a learned predictor can match or beat optimisation (Table 4: LaSOT 63.1 -> 64.7, LaSOTExtSub 43.7 -> 45.2) but also loses on UAV123 (67.7 -> 65.0) when only the classifier predictor is replaced; evidence that a recent confident frame helps localisation (Table 3: 65.7 -> 67.6 LaSOT) and that own pseudo-labels hurt the box branch (62.0 without two-stage). 5.1 (right object and refusal): caution - no explicit distractor or absence modelling; adding a learned background embedding hurts (Table 1 row 5). 5.3: indirect - all gains are from end-to-end training of a large backbone + predictor; no evidence for small fixed cores. 5.4: not addressed.
candidate_node_change: No primary candidate. A cheap design analogy that could be tested inside the existing readout (FlyVis readout node) without a Transformer: 'transductive target model' - when fitting the ridge target model, add the current search frame's map as unlabelled context (e.g. treat all current-crop locations far from the predicted center as additional background negatives, or re-fit after one self-labelled step) - mirrors ToMP's use of the test frame. Controls: same change on R1 input-eye features (no fly) and on stock C; compare with the current centered uniform ridge on D. Minimal check: train26 useful-center share, paired bootstrap by video. Stop condition: upper CI of change-on-D minus current D below +2 pp, or equal gain on R1/C (readout effect, not fly). Low priority: our search crop is about 2x target, so 'far from predicted center' negatives are few and the risk of declaring the true target as background after a large prediction error is high (cf. the 79.7 px R1 case).
strongest_objection: ToMP's improvement over the optimisation-based predictor is small and inconsistent (Table 4: +1.6 LaSOT, +0.4 NFS, -2.7 UAV123 when only the classifier predictor is replaced) and is obtained with a large RGB backbone, joint end-to-end training and global attention; the authors state that distractors during occlusion remain a typical failure. Our project's analogue of a learned predictor (pre-trained exemplar matching with absent class and negatives) already did not beat the online ridge readout, so adopting ToMP would repeat that experiment at higher cost with less data.
evidence_strength: Peer-reviewed (CVPR 2022), public code and models verified to exist in PyTracking, results reproduced and used as a baseline by later work (e.g. DiDi/DAM4SAM comparisons [uncertain]). Ablations: single training run per variant, no confidence intervals, evaluated on test sets. Overall: moderate - strong for RGB SOT benchmarks, weak for transfer to small motion features and to distractor-with-occlusion cases.
where_distinction_is_made: Target vs background: in the representation (target-location encoding added to training features; encoder features become target-aware) and in the predicted target model (DCF classifier trained with the DiMP classification loss: foreground regression, background hinge). Target vs similar distractor: implicit only, through the model and attention; no explicit distractor term (a learned background embedding was tried and hurt, Table 1 row 5). Target outside search area / not found: separate hand-set online rule copied from DiMP (tomp50.py: target_not_found_threshold 0.25, distractor ratio 0.8, hard-negative 0.5, search area rescaling at occlusion). Insufficient data: not modelled. Map maximum vs right object: only via the score threshold and second-peak ratio; memory update only when confidence > 0.9.
feature_dependence: Strongly depends on rich RGB appearance features (ResNet-50/101) and global self-attention across frames. No evidence for small motion/brightness features. The extent encoding is crucial (Table 1 row 7: 67.6 -> 63.1 LaSOT without it), i.e. the method relies on explicit box geometry tokens as well.
association_consequence: Not addressed (SOT). In our stand the output would enter as a center correction before matching; an external guard rule (shift limit relative to the Kalman prediction, cost check against the matching threshold) would remove harmful large corrections without any learned predictor, so any ToMP-like change must beat stand + guard rule.
difference_from_tried: Differences from our tried mechanisms: (1) learned feed-forward weight prediction instead of the closed-form online ridge model (we tried the ridge model: z13_target_model_probe_v1, z13_target_center_v1, z13_balanced_ridge_v1, z13_hinge_target_v1); (2) transductive use of the current search frame when predicting the model - not tried in our readout; (3) location + extent encoding injected into the features before joint processing - not tried; (4) memory of first + one high-confidence recent frame with separate trust per output (localisation vs box) - our observation memory (z13_observed_memory_v1) and query memory (z13_query_memory_v1) stored target observations without separating trust per output. Closest tried analogue: pre-trained exemplar matching with absent class and negatives (a learned, non-optimisation predictor) - so the core idea 'learned predictor instead of online fitting' is NOT new for the project; only (2) and (4) are untried design details.
memory_write_policy: Training set = annotated first frame (permanent) + at most one previous frame; the slot is replaced by the most recent frame whose classifier confidence exceeds a threshold (conf_ths 0.9 in tomp50.py). The pseudo-labelled frame is used for the classifier weights only; box-regression weights use only the annotated frame (two-stage inference, Sec. 3.5).
distractor_representation: Implicit only (via the classification loss and attention); no distractor buffer, track or class; learned background embedding tested and rejected (Table 1).
refusal_evidence_horizon: Single frame: score-map maximum and second-peak thresholds inherited from DiMP; memory write gated by a single-frame confidence threshold.
loss_on_applied_decision: No: classification loss on the test-frame score map plus GIoU on the predicted box; not on the arg-max decision, the not-found flag or memory writes.
association_entry_point: Not applicable in the source (SOT). For us it would be the same as the current Z13 entry point: center/box correction of the track prediction before matching.
no_fly_control_equivalent: Same predictor/transductive readout on input-eye features (R1, equal-dimension spatio-temporal filter bank) and on stock FlyVis C; plus Kalman-only stand with a shift-limit or matching-cost guard rule on corrections.
hard_subset_evaluation: LaSOTExtSub (150 videos of 15 new classes, small fast objects with distractors) reported separately; selected by the benchmark authors by class novelty, not by distractor density. LaSOT per-attribute analysis (Fig. 4) as a soft hard-subset view. No DiDi/DanceTrack evaluation.
temporal_information_availability: Causal: uses the first frame, one past frame and the current frame (transductively, unlabelled) - no future frames. Latency one forward pass (24.8 fps ResNet-50 on RTX 2080Ti). Benefit is available to a tracker acting now.
depth_level: Full analysis (code, ablations, all fields), as set in the item. Conclusion: source of explanation, not a basis for the next implementation; the core idea (learned predictor) repeats our failed exemplar-matching experiment.
